CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who presents with right elbow pain that started approximately one week ago while playing lacrosse with his children. He reports that his 13-year-old son struck him multiple times with a lacrosse stick during the game. Patient describes the pain as sharp, localized to the tip of the elbow, and radiating down the forearm. Pain occurs with any movement of the elbow. Patient took ibuprofen for a couple of days with some relief but has been inconsistent with use. Denies falling or direct recall of impact but acknowledges possible trauma from lacrosse stick contact. No associated chest pain or abdominal pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain. Denies abdominal pain. Lungs clear bilaterally. Heart sounds normal with known grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, previously documented.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Hypertension
2. Diabetes mellitus type 2
3. Systolic ejection murmur (grade 2/6)

MEDICATIONS
1. Lisinopril 20 mg daily
2. Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient plays lacrosse recreationally with his children, ages 13 and 10. Follows a Mediterranean diet with low salt intake as a family. Denies excessive salt intake.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure 150/90 mmHg
General: Alert and oriented
Cardiovascular: Heart exam shows grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, previously known
Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally
Right Elbow: Pain to palpation over olecranon area posteriorly. Mild pain with flexion and extension. Normal range of motion. Mild swelling and bruising noted.

RESULTS
Right elbow X-ray: No fracture, no bony abnormality, normal study.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right elbow contusion: Consistent with blunt trauma from lacrosse stick contact. Prescribed ibuprofen 800 mg twice daily for pain and inflammation. Recommend ice application three times daily for 20 minutes per session. Advise activity restriction—avoid playing lacrosse for the next couple of weeks to allow healing.
2. Hypertension: Blood pressure elevated today at 150/90, likely white coat syndrome. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Patient compliant with low-salt Mediterranean diet, which is beneficial. Will continue current management.
3. Diabetes mellitus type 2: Blood sugars well-controlled, ranging 80-100 mg/dL. Continue metformin 500 mg daily. Ordered hemoglobin A1c to assess glycemic control and determine if medication adjustment needed in future.
